newsitem.title: UK: Most N.Sea upstream assest in UK waters - Andersen.
newsitem.headline: Most N.Sea upstream assest in UK waters - Andersen.

text.p: Over 60 percent of the net value of remaining oil and gas assets in the North Sea are contained in fields on the U.K. Continental Shelf (UKCS), industry consultants Arthur Andersen Petroleum Services Group said on Tuesday.
Based on the value of fields in production, under development or with commercial potential, Andersen's report shows that 85 percent of the remaining value is held by the top 20 companies.
Royal Dutch/Shell leads the field, with British Petroleum (BP) and Exxon Corp following closely behind, Andersen said.
"Where almost all of BP's value is based in the U.K., Shell and Exxon tend to be more international with larger proportions in Norway, Netherlands and in Shell's case Denmark," the consultants said.
Norwegian producers were also beginning to diversify with Statoil holding commercial assets in Britain, Denmark and Ireland and Saga holding 25 percent of its asset value on the UKCS.
Of the major North Sea oil producing countries, Britain continues to have the most attractive fiscal regime with a marginal tax rate for new fields of 33 percent compared with Norway's 78 percent.
